To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
TGF-beta1 is converted to a mitogen by oncogenic activation of the Ras/Mitogen-activated protein (MAP) kinase pathway in prostate cancer.
the mitogenic conversion of TGF-beta by the oncogenic Ha-Ra signaling pathway in human prostrate cancer cells is due to the Smad-independent activation of p15 and p21.
TGF-beta1 has a growth-stimulatory effect in prostate cancer cell lines with oncogenic Ras mutation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel mechanism of TGF-beta action, which is mediated via the MAPK pathway, and provides a possible explanation for the paradoxical effect of TGF beta1 on tumor progression in prostate cancer.
the mechanism of TGF-beta action in prostate cancer cells.
the molecular mechanisms of TGF-beta signaling in the development of prostate cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the TGF-β signaling pathway is a complex one and the role of TGF-β in the prostate cancer cells is not a simple growth inhibition.
the oncogenic mutation of Ha-Ras in the prostate cancer cells can induce the conversion of TGF-beta from an antiproliferative to a proliferative growth factor by the Ras/MAP kinase pathway.

the oncogenic Ha-RAS induced mitogenic conversion of TGF-beta effect in the prostate cancer cells is mediated by the MAPK signaling pathway, whereas the TCF-beta1-induced growth arrest is maintained through the Smad signaling pathway.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

TGF-beta1 is a growth inhibitor in normal epithelial and prostate carcinoma cells, and that the oncogenic Ha-RAS-induced mitogenic conversion of TGF-beta action is mediated through activation of MAPK signaling pathway.
the TGFbeta1-mediated growth inhibition of prostate cancer can be converted to stimulation by activation of the MAPK signaling pathway.

oncogenic Ha-RaS can switch the TGF-beta effect from growth inhibition to stimulation by activation of the MAPK pathway, and that the Ras/MAPk pathway is a potential therapeutic target in prostate cancers with TGF-beta1 overexpression.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the TGF beta signaling pathway is altered in prostate cancer cells and the altered signaling pathway can lead to a loss of the growth inhibitory effects of TGF beta and the development of a mitogenic effect of this cytokine.
TGF-beta1 is not always an inhibitor of cell proliferation in prostate cancer.
TGF-beta1 may be a growth-promoting factor in prostate cancers with Ras/MAPK activation.
